findings.reason: a node could ship any change and still see base read 1, so the only control that shows the guard fires is unsound and the section must state the base reading it expects and the pointer fixture that produces it.
findings.text: §52's negative control ("the base revision, where the count equals the number of pointers") will not hold: `_env_scan_run_pid` already calls `_processes_owning_run(..., from_beat_map=True)` (`reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:1363`), whose `_beat_marked_processes` (`reckon/crew/process_signal.py:336-349`) walks the table once and reuses that map for `BEAT_SECONDS = 1.0`, so a 30-pointer refresh driven by a fast fake table finishes inside one beat and reads 1 at base, not 30; and `_env_scan_run_pid` is reached only when both the pointer pid and the worker-record pid have failed *and* a worker record exists, so "the count equals the number of pointers" additionally needs a fixture the section does not state — the gate as written measures nothing

findings.reason: the section as written declares the reported stall fixed on one half of its own evidence, and a reader would close it with the second hot path untouched.
findings.text: the Why names a second cost of the same stall ("In the other it is re-statting the review store through `_misfiled_review_candidates > _update_store_entries`"), which resolves to `reckon/crew/recovery_memo.py:370` and `reckon/crew/review_records.py:1430`; neither module is among the declared write paths (`process_signal.py`, `recovery_liveness.py`, `obligation_snapshot.py`, a new test file), and the done-when measures only process-table walks, so a node can satisfy this section while the station still stalls on the review-store re-stat the plan itself cites as part of the same 21-minute tick
